decisions.rationale: "breast/ovarian" is a contiguous string referring to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer) joined by a slash, analogous to the guideline's composite example, and it is used adjectivally for 'family'.

"breast / ovarian cancer" contiguously refers to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer) sharing the head term 'cancer', so it is one Composite Mention, used as a modifier of 'pedigree'.
"disease" is a very general term used only to say the family is affected by the disease, with no specific disease name, so it is excluded.
"breast cancer" is a disease name used as a modifier of the noun 'case' in 'bilateral breast cancer case', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
"breast tumour" refers to a breast cancer disease mention and modifies the noun 'pairs' in 'breast tumour / blood pairs'; 'tumour' is retained as a disease term.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 3 (Modifier); What NOT to Annotate 4 (tumor terms retained)

decisions.rationale: "tumours" used alone refers to tumours in general (a family of tumour diseases) rather than one specific disease with a single definition; 'tumour' is retained as a disease term, so it is annotated as a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 1 (Disease Class); What NOT to Annotate 4 (tumor terms retained)

decisions.rationale: In "tumour suppressor gene" the word 'tumour' names a class of genes, not a disease mention, so it should not be annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 (general terms) and 5 (non-disease biological concepts)

decisions.rationale: "disease" in "disease-bearing chromosome" is a very general term that does not name a specific disease, so it is excluded.
